name: Vegetable Poha
ingredients: 1 tbsp cold-pressed groundnut or sunflower oil
description: Traditional light breakfast of flattened rice gently tempered with mustard, turmeric, crunchy peanuts, and green peas.
recipe_steps: Rinse flattened rice in a colander under running water for 30 seconds until softened; drain completely and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat; add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add curry leaves, chopped green chillies, and diced potatoes; cook covered for 4 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
Add green peas, roasted peanuts, turmeric powder, and salt; stir well.
Gently fold in the rinsed poha. Cover and steam on very low flame for 2 to 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, drizzle fresh lemon juice, and garnish with chopped coriander before serving hot.
chef_tips: Do not soak poha in water or it will turn mushy. A gentle rinse in a colander is the secret to fluffy grains.

name: Steamed Idli with Sambar & Tomato Chutney
ingredients: 4 steamed fermented rice and black gram idlis
1 cup toor dal sambar with drumstick and carrots
2 tbsp fresh roasted tomato and red chilli chutney
description: Naturally fermented, gut-friendly steamed rice cakes served with protein-rich lentil vegetable sambar.
recipe_steps: Grease idli molds lightly and pour fermented rice-urad dal batter into each depression.
Steam in an idli cooker or steamer over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Simmer the pre-cooked toor dal with mixed vegetables, tamarind extract, and freshly grounded sambar powder for 8 minutes.
Prepare tomato chutney by sautéing tomatoes, cumin, and dry red chillies, then blending to a smooth dip.
Serve hot steamed idlis floating in a bowl of warm aromatic sambar with chutney on the side.
chef_tips: Steaming preserves nutrients and requires zero added cooking oil, making this exceptionally easy on digestion.

name: Moong Dal Cheela (Savory Lentil Crepe)
ingredients: 1/2 cup finely chopped capsicum and coriander
1 tsp olive or sunflower oil for cooking
description: High-protein golden crepes made from blended yellow split lentils with fresh herbs and bell peppers.
recipe_steps: Drain soaked moong dal and blend with ginger, green chilli, cumin seeds, and 3-4 tbsp water to a smooth pouring consistency.
Transfer batter to a bowl; whisk in turmeric, salt, and finely chopped capsicum.
Heat a cast iron skillet or non-stick tawa over medium flame; grease lightly with drops of oil.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread in concentric circles from the center outwards into a medium-thin crepe.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until golden brown crisp on the edges, flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.
Fold into a semi-circle and serve warm with mint-coriander dip.
chef_tips: Soak the yellow moong dal in warm water for 20 minutes if pressed for time.

name: Ragi Dosa with Coconut Mint Chutney
ingredients: 1 tsp sesame oil or sunflower oil
description: Calcium and iron-rich finger millet crisp crepes seasoned with onions, cumin, and fresh herbs.
recipe_steps: In a mixing bowl, combine ragi flour, rice flour, chopped onion, green chilli, curry leaves, cumin seeds, and salt.
Add water gradually while whisking to make a thin, buttermilk-like runny batter.
Rest the batter for 5-10 minutes.
Heat a tawa on high until very hot; splash water droplets to check.
Pour batter from the outer perimeter moving inwards without spreading with a ladle.
Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil along edges and cook on medium flame for 3 minutes until crisp, then flip for 30 seconds.
chef_tips: Ragi is rich in dietary fiber and slow-burning carbohydrates that support sustained morning stamina.

name: Greek Vegetable Omelette with Whole Wheat Toast
description: Mediterranean-inspired fluffy egg omelette folded with baby spinach, juicy cherry tomatoes, kalamata olives, and tangy feta.
recipe_steps: In a bowl, whisk whole eggs, egg white, oregano, black pepper, and a pinch of salt until frothy.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-low flame.
Sauté spinach and cherry tomatoes for 1 minute until spinach just wilts.
Pour the whisked eggs evenly over the vegetables. Cook undisturbed for 2 minutes until base sets.
Scatter crumbled feta and sliced olives over one half; fold the omelette gently.
Toast whole wheat bread until golden brown and serve alongside the warm omelette.
chef_tips: Whisking vigorously introduces micro air pockets that give the omelette a souffle-like velvety texture.

name: Cinnamon Apple Chia Oatmeal Bowl
ingredients: 1 cup almond milk or oat milk
description: Warm rolled oats simmered in plant milk with omega-rich chia seeds, spiced apple cubes, and toasted walnuts.
recipe_steps: Bring almond milk to a gentle simmer in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add rolled oats, chia seeds, and cinnamon powder; stir well to avoid clumping.
Lower heat to medium-low and simmer for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally until thick and creamy.
Transfer to a breakfast bowl; top with diced fresh apple, toasted walnuts, and a drizzle of maple syrup.
chef_tips: Chia seeds absorb liquid and form a gentle soluble fiber gel that keeps you feeling satisfied for hours.

name: Besan & Vegetable Masala Scramble
ingredients: 1/4 cup finely chopped bell peppers and tomatoes
1 tsp mustard oil or olive oil
description: Egg-free protein scramble prepared from spiced chickpea flour with carom seeds and colorful crunchy peppers.
recipe_steps: Whisk chickpea flour with water, turmeric, and salt until lump-free.
Heat oil in a skillet, add ajwain and chopped green chilli; let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Sauté chopped bell peppers and tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Pour the chickpea batter into the pan and continuously stir with a spatula over medium-low heat.
The batter will thicken and crumble into soft scramble curds over 4-5 minutes.
Garnish with coriander and serve warm.
chef_tips: Carom seeds (ajwain) enhance aromatic depth while assisting natural legume digestion.

name: Japanese Tofu & Miso Breakfast Soup with Brown Rice
ingredients: 1.5 cups vegetable dashi or mushroom broth
description: Comforting probiotic-rich fermented soybean soup with tender tofu cubes, nori, scallions, and warm brown rice.
recipe_steps: Heat vegetable broth in a pot until hot but not boiling.
Ladle 3 tbsp hot broth into a small bowl, whisk miso paste into it until completely dissolved.
Add diced tofu cubes and snipped nori to the pot; simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Remove pot from flame; stir the dissolved miso back into the pot (never boil miso directly).
Ladle soup over a small scoop of warm brown rice, drizzle sesame oil, and top with fresh spring onions.
chef_tips: Do not boil miso paste directly; adding it off the boil preserves the beneficial live probiotic cultures.

name: Boiled Egg Salad with Avocado Toast
ingredients: 1 thick slice whole-grain artisanal sourdough bread
Pinch of pink sea salt and crushed black pepper
description: Hearty whole-grain toast layered with creamy lemon-seasoned avocado, sliced boiled eggs, and peppery microgreens.
recipe_steps: Toast whole-grain sourdough bread in a toaster until crisp and deeply golden.
In a bowl, mash avocado with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Peel hard-boiled eggs and slice cleanly with a sharp knife.
Spread mashed avocado generously over the toasted bread.
Arrange egg slices over avocado; sprinkle red chilli flakes and microgreens.
chef_tips: Avocado provides heart-healthy monounsaturated fats that facilitate absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, and E from eggs.

name: Spinach & Paneer Paratha with Mint Curd
ingredients: 1 tsp ghee or oil for roasting
description: Vibrant emerald paratha kneaded with fresh spinach puree, stuffed with spiced low-fat paneer, served with cooling mint curd.
recipe_steps: Knead whole wheat flour with pureed spinach, ajwain, and a pinch of salt into a soft dough; rest for 10 minutes.
Season grated paneer with salt, green chilli, and garam masala.
Roll a small dough ball into a 4-inch disc, place 2 tbsp paneer filling in center, seal edges, and roll into a 7-inch paratha.
Cook on a hot skillet; apply 1/2 tsp ghee and roast both sides until golden speckles appear.
Serve warm with fresh curd beaten with chopped mint leaves.
chef_tips: Kneading spinach directly into the dough infuses natural folate and chlorophyll throughout every bite.

name: Mediterranean Chickpea & Quinoa Harvest Bowl
ingredients: 1 cup diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and bell peppers
2 tbsp chopped parsley and fresh mint
1 tbsp extra virgin cold-pressed olive oil
description: Wholesome gluten-free grain and pulse salad tossed with crunchy crisp garden vegetables, lemon, and extra virgin olive oil.
recipe_steps: In a wide salad bowl, combine cooked quinoa and tender boiled chickpeas.
Toss in diced cucumbers, sweet cherry tomatoes, and colorful bell peppers.
In a small glass jar, shake olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, oregano, and salt into an emulsion dressing.
Pour dressing over the bowl and toss lightly to coat every grain.
Garnish with chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley and mint.
chef_tips: Combining quinoa (a complete plant protein) with chickpeas provides all nine essential amino acids.

name: Yellow Dal Tadka with Steamed Brown Rice & Bhindi Masala
ingredients: 1 cup cooked yellow toor and masoor dal
1 cup stir-fried okra (bhindi) with onions and cumin
description: Classic Indian homestyle lunch of garlic-cumin tempered yellow lentils paired with fiber-rich brown rice and crisp okra stir-fry.
recipe_steps: Pressure cook or boil toor and masoor dal with turmeric and salt until tender.
Heat oil in a small pan; crackle cumin seeds, slit green chillies, and ginger.
Pour the fragrant tadka over the dal and simmer for 3 minutes.
Sauté sliced okra with cumin, coriander powder, and onion slices in 1/2 tsp oil until crisp and tender.
Serve warm dal over a mound of steamed brown rice with bhindi masala on the side.
chef_tips: Dry the okra thoroughly with a kitchen towel before slicing to prevent sliminess during cooking.

name: Grilled Lemon Herb Chicken with Roasted Sweet Potatoes
ingredients: 1 tbsp lemon juice & 1 tsp lemon zest
Crushed black pepper and sea salt
description: Tender grilled skinless chicken breast marinated in fresh citrus and herbs, balanced with sweet potato cubes and steamed greens.
recipe_steps: Pound chicken breast to even 1/2-inch thickness; marinate with olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, herbs, garlic powder, salt, and pepper for 10 minutes.
Toss sweet potato cubes with a few drops of oil and bake at 200°C for 18 minutes or pan-roast until caramelized and tender.
Heat a grill pan on medium-high; grill chicken fillets for 5-6 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 74°C.
Steam broccoli florets for 3 minutes until vibrant green yet crisp.
Rest chicken for 3 minutes to retain juices, slice and serve with sweet potato and broccoli.
chef_tips: Letting the cooked chicken rest for 3 minutes before slicing allows moisture to redistribute through the muscle fibers.

name: Tofu Teriyaki Stir-Fry with Jasmine Rice
ingredients: 130g extra firm organic tofu, pressed and cubed
1 cup mixed florets (broccoli, snow peas, sliced carrots)
3/4 cup cooked jasmine or brown rice
1.5 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce or tamari
1 tsp maple syrup or rice vinegar
description: Pan-seared golden tofu cubes glazed in a savory ginger-teriyaki glaze, tossed with crunchy vegetables over fragrant rice.
recipe_steps: Press tofu with a paper towel for 10 minutes to extract excess moisture; cut into 1-inch cubes.
Heat sesame oil in a wok; pan-sear tofu cubes until all sides are golden brown (about 6 minutes); remove.
In the same wok, flash fry sliced carrots, snow peas, and broccoli for 3 minutes.
Whisk low-sodium soy sauce, ginger, rice vinegar, and maple syrup; pour into the wok.
Return tofu to wok, toss in glaze for 1 minute until sticky and fragrant.
Serve over warm rice, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds.
chef_tips: Pressing the tofu beforehand ensures a crisp exterior that absorbs the savory teriyaki glaze without becoming soggy.

name: South Indian Curd Rice with Pomegranate & Cucumber
description: Cooling, creamy traditional South Indian rice blended with fresh curd, spiced with mustard tempering and sweet pomegranate.
recipe_steps: Mash warm soft-cooked rice gently with the back of a spoon.
Mix in fresh curd, diced cucumber, and salt until smooth and creamy.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a tadka ladle; add mustard seeds and curry leaves until they crackle.
Add ginger and green chilli; sauté for 15 seconds.
Pour tadka over curd rice and mix gently.
Top with fresh pomegranate seeds for a sweet, juicy burst of flavor.
chef_tips: Perfect for warm days or when digestion needs a soothing, gut-friendly lunch.

name: Grilled Fish Fillet with Lemon Butter Asparagus
ingredients: 140g fresh white fish fillet (cod, tilapia, or sea bass)
1/2 cup cooked brown rice or baby potatoes
1 tsp minced fresh dill or parsley
Pinch of garlic powder, sea salt, and crushed peppercorn
description: Pan-grilled white fish fillet seasoned with fresh dill, cracked peppercorns, and lemon, served with tender asparagus spears.
recipe_steps: Pat fish fillet dry with paper towels; season both sides with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and lemon zest.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with 1/2 tbsp butter and a few drops of oil.
Place fish skin-side down; sear for 4 minutes until golden, flip and cook 3 minutes until opaque and flaky.
In the same pan, toss asparagus spears with remaining butter and lemon juice for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Plate fish and asparagus alongside brown rice, garnished with fresh dill.
chef_tips: Drying fish thoroughly prevents steaming and guarantees a delicate, golden-brown sear.

name: Paneer Tikka with Mint Chutney & Whole Wheat Roti
ingredients: 1/2 cup bell pepper cubes and red onions
1/2 tsp chaat masala and Kashmiri red chilli powder
description: Tandoori-spiced char-grilled paneer skewers tossed with capsicum and red onions, served with soft chapatis and mint chutney.
recipe_steps: In a bowl, mix hung curd, mustard oil, besan, Kashmiri chilli, kasuri methi, and chaat masala into a marinade.
Toss paneer cubes, capsicum, and onions gently in the marinade; coat thoroughly.
Thread onto skewers or arrange on a hot grill pan; cook for 3 minutes per side until charred on edges.
Dust with a pinch of chaat masala.
Serve warm with freshly rolled whole wheat rotis and mint coriander chutney.
chef_tips: Mustard oil in tandoori marinades imparts that authentic smoky restaurant flavor without requiring deep frying.

name: Egg Fried Brown Rice with Spring Vegetables
ingredients: 1/2 cup finely diced carrots, green peas, and scallions
description: Wok-tossed whole grain brown rice with fluffy scrambled eggs, sweet green peas, carrots, and toasted sesame aromatics.
recipe_steps: Heat 1/2 tsp sesame oil in a wok on high heat; pour beaten eggs, scramble quickly into soft ribbons, and remove.
Add remaining oil to wok; stir-fry diced carrots, peas, and green chilli for 2 minutes on high flame.
Add cold cooked brown rice, breaking up any clumps with a wooden spatula.
Drizzle soy sauce and white pepper around the sides of the wok; toss vigorously for 2 minutes.
Fold in the cooked egg ribbons and chopped scallions; toss once and serve piping hot.
chef_tips: Using refrigerated day-old rice keeps the grains firm and distinctly separated during wok stir-frying.

name: Jain Yellow Lentil Khichdi with Steamed Zucchini
ingredients: 1 cup diced zucchini and green peas (root-free)
1 tsp sesame oil or cold-pressed oil
description: Strict root-vegetable-free comforting one-pot preparation of rice and split moong lentils with cumin and zucchini.
recipe_steps: Wash rice and yellow moong dal together; drain thoroughly.
Heat ghee or oil in a pressure cooker; temper cumin seeds and asafoetida for 10 seconds.
Add diced zucchini, green peas, turmeric powder, and rock salt.
Add the rinsed rice and dal, followed by 3.5 cups of water.
Pressure cook on medium heat for 3 whistles; let steam release naturally.
Whisk gently with a ladle for a velvety comfort-food texture.
chef_tips: A gentle wholesome meal strictly complying with traditional Jain dietary guidelines with no onion, garlic, or root tubers.

name: Mediterranean Falafel Mezze Salad with Hummus
ingredients: 1.5 cups mixed salad greens, cucumbers, and kalamata olives
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil and lemon juice dressing
description: Crispy oven-baked herb falafels nestled on leafy salad greens, served with rich tahini hummus and lemon-olive oil dressing.
recipe_steps: Bake herb chickpea falafels on a parchment-lined tray at 190°C for 15 minutes until golden and crisp.
Spread creamy tahini hummus along one side of a wide salad bowl.
Assemble crisp mixed lettuce, cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, and kalamata olives.
Arrange the warm baked falafels on top of the greens.
Drizzle with cold-pressed olive oil, lemon juice, and a dusting of tangy sumac.
chef_tips: Baking falafels instead of deep-frying reduces excessive saturated fats while delivering a satisfying crunch.

name: Slow-Simmered Chicken Soup with Carrots and Barley
ingredients: 2.5 cups rich aromatic chicken or vegetable broth
1 bay leaf and 1 sprig fresh thyme
Sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
description: Restorative, soothing clear broth simmered with tender lean chicken, fiber-dense pearled barley, and aromatic sweet garden vegetables.
recipe_steps: In a heavy soup pot, bring chicken broth to a gentle rolling boil.
Add pearled barley, sliced carrots, celery, bay leaf, and fresh thyme.
Lower heat to medium-low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until barley softens.
Add diced chicken breast; simmer gently for another 10 minutes until chicken is tender and thoroughly cooked.
Discard bay leaf; adjust seasoning with sea salt and cracked black pepper.
Ladle steaming hot into deep bowls and garnish with fresh parsley.
chef_tips: Barley releases wholesome beta-glucan fibers that naturally thicken the broth without needing cream or cornstarch.

name: Methi Matar Malai (Low-Fat) with Phulkas
ingredients: 1 cup fresh fenugreek leaves (methi), washed and chopped
1/4 cup blended low-fat milk and cashew paste
description: Delicately spiced mild curry of sweet green peas and slightly bitter fenugreek leaves in a wholesome light cashew-milk gravy.
recipe_steps: Sprinkle a pinch of salt on chopped methi leaves; squeeze out bitter water after 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan; temper cumin seeds and slit green chilli.
Add squeezed methi leaves and green peas; sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in blended cashew and low-fat milk mixture; stir continuously on low heat until gently bubbling.
Season with garam masala and salt; simmer for 4 minutes until luscious.
Serve hot with freshly puffed oil-free whole wheat phulkas.
chef_tips: Fenugreek supports glycemic balance and pairs harmoniously with sweet green peas.

name: Baked Herb Crusted Salmon with Green Beans
ingredients: 1 cup fresh french green beans, trimmed
1 tbsp Dijon mustard and lemon juice
1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley and dill
Flaky sea salt and black pepper
description: Omega-3 rich wild salmon baked to tender perfection with an aromatic herb mustard crust, paired with crisp green beans.
recipe_steps: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F); line a baking tray with foil.
Brush salmon top with Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and chopped herbs; season with salt and pepper.
Toss green beans with olive oil and place alongside salmon on the baking tray.
Bake for 12-14 minutes until salmon flakes easily with a fork and green beans are blistered and tender.
Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and serve with roasted baby potatoes.
chef_tips: Rich in marine omega-3 fatty acids (EPA & DHA) which support post-workout muscle recovery and cellular wellness.

name: Vegetable Sambar Rice with Roasted Appalam
ingredients: 1.5 cups aromatic sambar loaded with pumpkin, carrots, and shallots
Curry leaves and mustard seed seasoning
description: South Indian staple comfort dinner of slow-simmered lentil stew and soft rice infused with vegetables and tempered spices.
recipe_steps: Combine cooked rice and piping hot vegetable sambar in a pot.
Simmer together for 3-4 minutes so the rice absorbs the tangy tamarind and lentil flavours.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in 1 tsp coconut oil; pour over the dish.
Roast a lentil papad directly on the open flame or microwave for 30 seconds until crisp.
Serve warm.
chef_tips: A light evening meal that is comforting and easy on nocturnal digestion.

name: Steamed Edamame & Vegetable Brown Rice Noodles
ingredients: 1 cup julienned cabbage, bell peppers, and bok choy
description: Gluten-free brown rice noodles tossed in a wok with protein-rich young edamame beans, crunchy bok choy, and ginger tamari.
recipe_steps: Soak brown rice noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes; drain and rinse with cold water.
Heat sesame oil in a wok; toss grated ginger, julienned cabbage, and bok choy over high heat for 2 minutes.
Add shelled edamame and pour in tamari sauce.
Add noodles to the wok; toss gently with tongs for 2 minutes until evenly coated and heated through.
Garnish with sliced scallions and serve hot.
chef_tips: Edamame is a whole soy food providing a complete amino acid profile without cholesterol.

name: Grilled Paneer & Roasted Vegetable Couscous
ingredients: 1 cup roasted zucchini, bell peppers, and red onion
description: Fluffy whole grain couscous tossed with Mediterranean roasted vegetables and golden pan-grilled cottage cheese cubes.
recipe_steps: Pour boiling water over whole wheat couscous in a bowl, cover with a plate, and steam for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Toss diced zucchini, bell peppers, and onions with 1/2 tsp olive oil, oregano, and salt; roast or sauté until caramelized.
Pan-sear paneer cubes on a non-stick griddle for 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Combine warm couscous with roasted vegetables and paneer.
Drizzle with lemon juice and remaining olive oil before serving.
chef_tips: Couscous steams in just 5 minutes without needing active stovetop cooking.

name: Lauki (Bottle Gourd) & Chana Dal Curry with Multigrain Roti
description: Light, highly hydrating bottle gourd stewed with split Bengal gram dal, mild cumin, and served with rustic multigrain chapatis.
recipe_steps: Heat oil in a pressure cooker; splutter cumin seeds.
Add diced lauki, soaked chana dal, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Add 1 cup water, close the lid, and cook for 3 whistles on medium flame.
Release pressure naturally; simmer open for 2 minutes to achieve desired consistency.
Serve warm with hot multigrain rotis.
chef_tips: Bottle gourd has high water content and low caloric density, making it ideal for a relaxing evening meal.

name: Grilled Prawns with Garlic Herb Cauliflower Rice
ingredients: Crushed red pepper flakes and sea salt
description: Succulent garlic-herb grilled prawns served atop a fluffy, aromatic base of low-carb sautéed cauliflower rice.
recipe_steps: Toss cleaned prawns with 1/2 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, lemon juice, salt, and red pepper flakes.
Sauté remaining garlic in olive oil in a pan; add riced cauliflower and sauté for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
In a separate skillet or grill, sear prawns on high heat for 1.5 to 2 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Season cauliflower rice with salt and freshly chopped parsley.
Serve hot prawns placed gracefully over the warm cauliflower rice.
chef_tips: Prawns cook in under 4 minutes; remove from flame as soon as they turn opaque to keep them tender.

name: Creamy Tuscan White Bean & Tomato Stew
ingredients: 1.5 cups boiled cannellini or navy white beans
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
description: Rustic Italian comfort stew of creamy white cannellini beans simmered with rich tomatoes, fragrant herbs, and wilted baby spinach.
recipe_steps: Heat olive oil in a saucepan; add rosemary and basil to bloom aromatics.
Pour in crushed tomatoes; simmer for 5 minutes until reduced slightly.
Add boiled cannellini beans with 1/4 cup of their cooking liquid; season with salt and pepper.
Simmer on medium-low for 6-8 minutes until rich and thick.
Stir in baby spinach leaves until just wilted.
Ladle into a warm bowl and finish with a drizzle of virgin olive oil.
chef_tips: Cannellini beans are packed with prebiotic soluble fiber that supports gut flora and metabolic health.

name: Steamed Vegetable Momos with Spicy Tomato Sesame Dip
ingredients: 6 freshly steamed vegetable dumplings (cabbage, carrot, mushroom filling)
2 tbsp roasted tomato, garlic, and toasted sesame seed chutney
1 cup clear vegetable broth on the side
Pinch of Sichuan pepper and Himalayan salt
description: Delicate steamed Himalayan dumplings stuffed with finely minced vegetables, served with a zesty tomato sesame dip and warm broth.
recipe_steps: Roll thin wrappers from whole wheat or unbleached flour dough.
Stuff with finely grated cabbage, carrots, ginger, and a pinch of salt; pleat tightly.
Place momos in a greased steamer basket.
Steam over boiling water for 10 minutes until skins become translucent and non-sticky.
Serve warm with freshly pounded spicy tomato-sesame dip.
chef_tips: Steaming preserves the delicate crunch and water-soluble vitamins of the minced vegetable filling.

name: Roasted Masala Makhana (Foxnuts)
ingredients: 1 tsp cold-pressed olive or groundnut oil
description: Crunchy, low-calorie popped lotus seeds roasted with turmeric, chaat masala, and pink rock salt.
recipe_steps: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed kadai or skillet over low heat.
Add makhana and roast continuously on low flame for 5-6 minutes until crispy.
Turn off the heat; immediately sprinkle turmeric, chaat masala, and pink salt.
Toss thoroughly so spices adhere to the warm seeds.
Allow to cool slightly for maximum crunch.
chef_tips: Makhana is low in sodium and high in magnesium, making it an ideal post-movement light snack.

name: Sprouted Moong & Pomegranate Chaat
ingredients: 1/4 cup finely chopped cucumber and tomatoes
description: Refreshing raw sprout salad bursting with tangy lemon juice, crunchy cucumber, sweet ruby pomegranate, and mint.
recipe_steps: Steam green moong sprouts for 2 minutes to soften them slightly while keeping them crisp.
In a bowl, combine warm sprouts, cucumber, tomatoes, and pomegranate seeds.
Season with roasted cumin powder, black salt, and minced green chilli.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice, toss well, and finish with chopped coriander.
chef_tips: Sprouting enhances protein bioavailability and multiplies vitamin C content significantly.

name: Greek Yogurt Parfait with Mixed Berries & Almonds
ingredients: 3/4 cup strained low-fat unsweetened Greek yogurt
description: Thick protein-rich strained yogurt layered with antioxidant-packed berries, raw honey, and crisp toasted almonds.
recipe_steps: Stir vanilla extract into thick Greek yogurt.
In a glass or bowl, place half the yogurt.
Add a layer of mixed fresh berries.
Top with remaining yogurt, sliced almonds, and a drizzle of honey.
Enjoy immediately chilled.
chef_tips: Strained Greek yogurt delivers twice the protein of regular curd and keeps you satiated between meals.

name: Boiled Chickpea Sundal with Grated Coconut
description: South Indian temple-style seasoned chickpeas tempered with fragrant coconut oil, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and fresh grated coconut.
recipe_steps: Heat coconut oil in a pan; add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add dry red chilli, curry leaves, and asafoetida.
Add boiled chickpeas and salt; toss for 2-3 minutes over medium heat.
Turn off flame, fold in fresh grated coconut, and serve warm.
chef_tips: Coconut oil and curry leaves provide an authentic South Indian aroma with minimal added fat.

name: Steamed Edamame Pods with Sea Salt
ingredients: 1.5 cups whole green edamame pods (in shell)
1/2 tsp coarse sea salt or Himalayan pink salt
description: Warm, tender young whole soybean pods steamed fresh and sprinkled with coarse flaky sea salt.
recipe_steps: Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a pot with a steamer basket.
Add whole edamame pods; cover and steam for 5 minutes.
Drain well and transfer to a serving bowl.
Sprinkle coarse sea salt and sesame seeds over warm pods.
Squeeze beans directly from pods into mouth and discard shells.
chef_tips: Fun to eat, nutrient-dense, and naturally packed with plant protein and fiber.

name: Apple Slices with Natural Peanut Butter
ingredients: 1 crisp medium apple (Honeycrisp or Gala), cored and sliced
1.5 tbsp 100% natural roasted peanut butter (no added sugar/hydrogenated oil)
description: Crunchy fresh apple wedges paired with wholesome stone-ground peanut butter dusted with aromatic cinnamon.
recipe_steps: Wash and core the apple; slice into 12 even wedges.
Spoon natural peanut butter into a small ramekin.
Dust cinnamon over peanut butter.
Dip apple wedges and enjoy immediately.
chef_tips: Pairing soluble fiber from apples with healthy fats in peanut butter blunts glucose spikes and sustains focus.

name: Cucumber & Carrot Sticks with Roasted Garlic Hummus
ingredients: 1 cup English cucumber and sweet carrot batons
3 tbsp authentic roasted garlic and tahini chickpea hummus
1/2 tsp extra virgin olive oil drizzle
description: Hydrating, crisp vegetable sticks served with smooth tahini-infused roasted garlic chickpea dip.
recipe_steps: Cut peeled carrots and cucumbers into 3-inch finger batons.
Ladle hummus into a shallow bowl, drizzle with olive oil and dust with paprika.
Arrange vegetable sticks around the dip and serve chilled.
chef_tips: Pre-cut veggies kept in a jar of water in the fridge stay crunchy for up to 3 days.

name: Roasted Masala Peanuts with Onions and Lime
description: Zesty street-style dry roasted peanut chaat tossed with fresh red onions, green chillies, lime juice, and coriander.
recipe_steps: In a bowl, combine roasted peanuts with finely diced onions and tomatoes.
Add green chilli, chaat masala, and a pinch of salt.
Squeeze fresh lime juice over the mixture and toss immediately.
Garnish with chopped coriander and serve right away so peanuts stay crunchy.
chef_tips: Toss with lime juice right before serving to keep the roasted peanuts supremely crisp.

name: Chia Seed & Coconut Milk Pudding with Mango
ingredients: 1/2 cup light coconut milk or almond milk
1/3 cup diced fresh mango or berries
description: Silky chilled coconut milk pudding set naturally with chia seeds, topped with juicy tropical sweet mango cubes.
recipe_steps: Whisk chia seeds, coconut milk, vanilla, and maple syrup together in a small mason jar.
Rest for 10 minutes, whisk again to break any clumps, and chill in refrigerator for at least 30 minutes (or overnight).
Top with freshly diced sweet mango cubes or seasonal berries before serving.
chef_tips: Whisking twice within the first 10 minutes prevents seeds from sinking to the bottom of the jar.

name: Hard-Boiled Egg with Paprika and Sea Salt
ingredients: Flaky sea salt and crushed black pepper
description: Pure, simple bioavailable protein: a perfectly hard-boiled egg dusted with fragrant smoked paprika and sea salt.
recipe_steps: Lower egg gently into a pot of boiling water; simmer for 9 minutes for firm yet tender yolk.
Transfer to an ice water bath for 3 minutes to halt cooking and ease peeling.
Peel shell, slice egg in half lengthwise, and dust with smoked paprika, sea salt, and black pepper.
chef_tips: Plunging the egg into ice water creates a temperature shock that separates the inner membrane from the shell.

name: Baked Tofu Bites with Sweet Chilli Soy Dip
ingredients: 1 tbsp sweet chilli sauce with a splash of rice vinegar
description: Crispy oven-baked tofu nuggets with a delicate golden crust, served with a tangy sweet chilli dip.
recipe_steps: Pat tofu cubes dry with a cloth; toss with soy sauce and sesame oil, then dust lightly with cornstarch.
Arrange on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, flipping halfway until crispy and golden.
Serve warm with sweet chilli dipping sauce.
chef_tips: Dusting tofu cubes with a touch of cornstarch creates a delightfully crisp exterior without deep frying.

name: Classic Dal Palak (Spinach Lentils) with Jeera Rice
ingredients: 1 cup cooked yellow toor and moong dal
description: Hearty iron-rich spinach stewed together with split yellow lentils, tempered with fragrant cumin seeds and served over fluffy jeera rice.
recipe_steps: Cook dal with turmeric and salt until soft.
Heat oil in a pan, splutter cumin seeds.
Add washed and chopped spinach; cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Pour in cooked dal, stir well, add garam masala, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed cumin-scented rice.
chef_tips: Adding a squeeze of fresh lemon juice right before eating enhances iron absorption from the spinach.

name: Mediterranean Tuna & White Bean Salad
ingredients: 1/2 cup diced red onion, celery, and cherry tomatoes
1 tbsp red wine vinegar or lemon juice
Fresh chopped parsley, sea salt, and black pepper
description: Quick, no-cook high-protein Mediterranean salad combining flaked wild tuna, tender white beans, and crunchy garden celery in lemon dressing.
recipe_steps: Drain canned tuna and flake into bite-sized chunks with a fork.
In a bowl, combine flaked tuna, drained white beans, diced celery, red onion, and cherry tomatoes.
Whisk olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper into a vinaigrette.
Pour dressing over salad, toss gently, and garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
chef_tips: A convenient zero-cooking lunch option packed with clean protein and complex dietary fiber.

name: Warm Roasted Tomato Basil Soup with Whole Grain Croutons
ingredients: 1 slice whole grain bread, toasted and cubed
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
description: Slow-roasted vine-ripened tomatoes simmered with fresh aromatic sweet basil, puréed silky smooth with crunchy homemade whole grain croutons.
recipe_steps: Roast halved tomatoes in a hot skillet with olive oil until skins blister and sweeten.
Transfer tomatoes and vegetable broth to a pot; simmer for 8 minutes.
Add fresh basil leaves and blend with an immersion blender until velvety.
Season with sea salt and cracked black pepper.
Toast whole grain bread cubes in a pan; float on top of hot soup.
chef_tips: Roasting tomatoes deepens their natural sweetness and unlocks lycopene, a potent antioxidant.

name: Peanut Butter & Banana High-Calorie Oats Bowl
ingredients: 1.5 cups whole milk or soy milk
1 tbsp organic honey or maple syrup
description: Rich calorie-dense energy bowl formulated for muscle growth and healthy weight gaining with healthy fats and complex carbs.
recipe_steps: Simmer rolled oats in whole milk or soy milk for 4-5 minutes until thick and creamy.
Pour hot oatmeal into a serving bowl; stir in honey and 1 tbsp peanut butter.
Top with sliced ripe bananas, roasted almonds, chia seeds, and dollop remaining peanut butter on top.
chef_tips: For an extra 100 calories, blend with 2 soaked Medjool dates or drizzle extra crushed walnuts.

name: Loaded Paneer & Cashew Brown Rice Pulao
ingredients: 150g firm paneer, diced into golden seared cubes
1 whole cinnamon stick, 2 green cardamoms, 1 bay leaf
description: Hearty North Indian aromatic brown rice dish packed with golden ghee-seared paneer cubes, roasted cashews, and sweet peas.
recipe_steps: Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan; lightly sear paneer cubes until golden on all sides, then set aside.
In the same pan, heat remaining ghee, add whole spices (cinnamon, cardamom, bay leaf) and allow to release aroma.
Add green peas, cumin powder, and roasted cashews; saute for 2 minutes.
Fold in cooked brown rice and seared paneer cubes gently; sprinkle salt and 2 tbsp warm water, cover and steam for 3 minutes on low flame.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander and serve warm.
chef_tips: Using desi ghee provides easily absorbed short-chain fatty acids that facilitate caloric density without heavy feeling.

name: Whole-Wheat Chicken, Avocado & Hummus Power Wrap
ingredients: 1 cup fresh baby spinach and sliced cucumbers
Pinch of smoked paprika and sea salt
description: High-protein powerhouse wrap pairing lean grilled chicken breast with monounsaturated healthy fats from avocado and tahini hummus.
recipe_steps: Warm the whole-wheat tortillas on a dry skillet for 20 seconds each.
Spread 1.5 tbsp hummus across each tortilla base.
Layer with fresh baby spinach, sliced cucumbers, warm grilled chicken strips, and avocado slices.
Drizzle lightly with extra virgin olive oil, sprinkle smoked paprika, roll tightly, and slice diagonally.
chef_tips: Avocado and olive oil add healthy calories and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) that aid post-workout recovery.

name: Hearty Moong Dal & Oats Khichdi with Ghee & Almonds
ingredients: 3/4 cup yellow moong dal (split yellow lentils)
description: Comforting, nutrient-dense wholesome khichdi uniting protein-rich moong dal and fiber-rich oats tempered with aromatic ghee and almonds.
recipe_steps: Rinse moong dal and oats together under cold water; drain.
Heat 1.5 tbsp ghee in a pressure cooker or heavy pot; add cumin seeds, hing, and grated ginger.
Add turmeric powder, moong dal, oats, salt, and 3 cups of water.
Cook for 3 whistles in pressure cooker (or simmer covered 18 mins on stove) until smooth and porridge-like.
Stir in remaining ghee and top with roasted crushed almonds before serving.
chef_tips: Extremely soothing on the digestive tract while providing a solid 580 calories and 24g of bioavailable plant protein.

name: Greek Yogurt, Dried Fig, Walnut & Honey Parfait
ingredients: 1.5 cups thick strained whole-milk Greek yogurt
description: Luxurious Mediterranean parfait layering protein-dense Greek yogurt with omega-3 rich walnuts, crunchy granola, and sweet dried figs.
recipe_steps: Spoon half of the Greek yogurt into a wide bowl or mason jar.
Layer with chopped dried figs, granola, and half of the walnuts.
Add the remaining yogurt, drizzle generously with honey, and garnish with remaining walnuts and pumpkin seeds.
chef_tips: A phenomenal pre-bedtime or post-workout snack providing slow-digesting casein protein that feeds muscles overnight.

name: Tofu, Sweet Potato & Quinoa Bowl with Creamy Tahini
ingredients: 180g extra firm tofu, cubed and pan-crisped
1 medium roasted sweet potato, cut into chunks
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice & 1 tbsp warm water
Sea salt, garlic powder & smoked paprika
description: Complete plant-based hypertrophy dinner bowl delivering complete amino acids from quinoa, beans, and crispy tofu with rich sesame fats.
recipe_steps: Toss tofu cubes with olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and salt; pan-sear in skillet for 8 minutes until all sides are crispy.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, salt, and warm water in a small ramekin until smooth and pourable.
Assemble bowl with a base of warm quinoa, roasted sweet potatoes, black beans, and crispy tofu.
Drizzle generously with creamy tahini dressing and enjoy.
chef_tips: Combining quinoa and black beans delivers all 9 essential amino acids with exceptional micronutrient density.
